ai.definition: Photovoltaic panels that convert sunlight directly into electricity using crystalline silicon cells.
ai.howItWorks: Purified silicon is cast into ingots, sliced into wafers, doped to form a p–n junction, then assembled into glass-covered modules with anti-reflective coatings.
ai.problemSolved: Generation of clean, renewable electricity from sunlight.
ai.manufacturing: Silicon purification, casting, wafering, doping, module assembly.
ai.buildProcess: Purification, casting, slicing, doping, cell production, module assembly, anti-reflective coating application.
ai.costDrivers: Silicon raw material cost, manufacturing equipment and labor, energy consumption during production, quality control measures.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: continuing growth with advancements in efficiency and cost reduction.
ai.regulation: Varies by region; often includes incentives for renewable energy adoption.
ai.risks: Supply chain disruptions, technological obsolescence, environmental impact of manufacturing processes.
ai.profitability: High due to decreasing costs and increasing demand, but margins can be thin.
ai.futureDevelopment: Focus on efficiency improvements, recycling silicon materials, reducing production costs, and integrating with energy storage solutions.

glossary.def: A semiconductor interface where the p-type (positive) and n-type (negative) regions meet to facilitate the flow of current.
A thin layer applied to the surface of solar cells to minimize light reflection, increasing absorption and efficiency.

subsystems.name: Silicon cells
subsystems.role: turn sunlight into electric current at a p–n junction.

subsystems.name: Module package
subsystems.role: protects the cells outdoors for 25–30+ years.

subsystems.name: Mounting
subsystems.role: holds modules at the right angle; single-axis trackers follow the sun for more energy.

subsystems.name: Inverters and power electronics
subsystems.role: convert DC to grid-compatible AC and keep each string at its maximum power point.

subsystems.name: Balance of system
subsystems.role: wiring, protection and monitoring that tie it together.

buildSteps.title: Purify the silicon
buildSteps.detail: Quartz is reduced to metallurgical silicon in an arc furnace, then refined into polysilicon of extreme purity — mostly by the Siemens chemical-vapour process.

buildSteps.title: Grow crystal ingots
buildSteps.detail: Polysilicon is melted with a trace of dopant and a single crystal is slowly pulled from the melt (the Czochralski method).

buildSteps.title: Slice wafers
buildSteps.detail: Diamond-wire saws cut the ingot into wafers roughly 0.15 mm thick; thinner wafers save silicon but crack more easily.

buildSteps.title: Make the cells
buildSteps.detail: The surface is etched into tiny pyramids to trap light, dopants are diffused in to form the junction, passivation and anti-reflective layers are deposited, and silver contacts are screen-printed and fired.

buildSteps.title: Test and sort
buildSteps.detail: Every cell is flash-tested and binned by output so matched cells go into the same module.

buildSteps.title: Assemble modules
buildSteps.detail: Cells are soldered into strings, laminated between glass and encapsulant under heat and vacuum, then framed and fitted with a junction box.

buildSteps.title: Quality-check modules
buildSteps.detail: A flash test sets the power rating and electroluminescence imaging reveals micro-cracks invisible to the eye.

buildSteps.title: Build the farm
buildSteps.detail: Piles and racking go in, modules are mounted and wired into strings, strings feed inverters, and a substation connects the farm to the grid.

pathway.unlocks: higher efficiency from better surface passivation, on the same production lines.

pathway.unlocks: more energy per hectare, which matters as good land gets scarcer.

pathway.unlocks: growth without hitting a silver shortage or a waste problem at end of life.
